slides.title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that integrating belief propagation with opinion dynamics, while maintaining coherence through shared values, increases the formation of echo chambers. This insight is relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies by highlighting how multi-scale belief-opinion interactions can drive societal segregation.

card.one_liner: Coherent belief-opinion propagation increases echo chamber count but reduces involved agents.
card.key_idea: Extends opinion dynamics with belief merging and coherence constraints to analyze joint propagation effects on echo chamber formation.
card.evaluation: Simulations with varying initial conditions and tolerances; uses stricter measures to confirm echo chambers in beliefs and opinions.
card.limitation: Results rely on simulation settings; real-world applicability of coherence constraints and specific merge operations remains unverified.

slides.title: SkillLens: Action-Guided Dense Visual Dynamics for Proficiency Estimation
slides.highlight: SkillLens bridges the gap between sensor-level evidence and abstract proficiency labels by using atomic action descriptions to localize proficiency-relevant windows for dense visual-dynamics extraction, aligning with MOSAIC's goal of estimating human proficiency from ego-exo views.

card.one_liner: SkillLens estimates human proficiency by comparing dense visual dynamics in action windows against expert and novice prototypes.
card.key_idea: Uses atomic action descriptions to localize windows, computes high-low prototype margins on visual dynamics, and fuses with ego-exo-gaze features via CORAL ordinal calibration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Ego-Exo4D; achieves 0.542 accuracy, outperforming baselines like SkillSight, with ablations confirming component contributions.
card.limitation: Performance suffers in activity-action buckets with severe class imbalance or missing proficiency levels, limiting prototype construction.

slides.title: Realbotix launches humanoid robots for education, wellness and companionship
slides.highlight: Realbotix's launch of humanoid robots for education, wellness, and companionship highlights the growing commercial focus on social robotics, a domain central to RwB's exploration of embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Neon AI Model
slides.highlight: Google has released the Gemini 4 Neon AI model, which is positioned as a rival to Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol.

slides.title: Public-Private Cooperation in the Port of Rotterdam: An Agent-Based Toy Model of Cooperative Efforts Against Cocaine Trafficking
slides.highlight: This study uses an agent-based model to analyze public-private cooperation dynamics, demonstrating that coordinated multi-parameter strategies significantly outperform isolated measures in complex governance systems.

card.one_liner: Agent-based modeling shows coordinated multi-parameter strategies outperform isolated measures in port security cooperation.
card.key_idea: Coupled ABM and CLD explore trust, cooperation, and enforcement dynamics, highlighting state-dependent effectiveness in public-private port security.
card.evaluation: Simulated parameter shocks over five years using empirical Rotterdam data; coordinated strategies yielded 25% effectiveness gain versus 13% for isolated measures.
card.limitation: Exploratory toy model lacking validation against real-world test cases or additional expert input.

slides.title: Embodied Interaction Policy: A Unified Model for Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Embodied Interaction Policy (EIP), a unified streaming framework that couples speech and motion generation through joint attention to enable continuous, interruption-aware full-duplex human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots by demonstrating how state-adaptive and emotion-conditioned behavior can improve interaction naturalness and reduce latency in real-time social contexts.

card.one_liner: EIP unifies speech and motion generation via joint attention for low-latency, full-duplex human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Couples a frozen audio-interaction expert with a motion expert using layer-wise joint attention and a vocal token for state-aware, emotion-conditioned streaming generation.
card.evaluation: Trained on EI-Data; evaluated via motion metrics, user studies, and physical deployment on Astribot S1, showing improved quality and 64% lower latency.
card.limitation: Relies solely on audio input, limiting the ability to interpret visual cues like gaze, facial expressions, and body posture.

slides.title: Ant Division of Labor Models Enable Autonomous Multi-Agent Role Allocation
slides.highlight: Research on ant division of labor models informs autonomous role allocation in multi-agent systems, relevant to MIMIC's development of agent models for hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: NVIDIA Unveils GR00T 2 and Other Robot Technologies at CoRL Conference
slides.highlight: NVIDIA released GR00T 2 and other robot technologies at the CoRL Conference.

slides.title: Microsoft releases Aion, a small open model for Windows integration
slides.highlight: Microsoft has published Aion, a small open-weight model intended for integration into Windows by January.

slides.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that integrates gaze geometry with speech transcripts and speaker identification to resolve ambiguity in multi-party attention, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Nunchi combines gaze geometry with conversational cues via a VLM to accurately identify attended persons in multi-party scenes.
card.key_idea: Constructs text prompts from gaze heatmaps, speaker scores, and transcripts, using shared labels to align cues and a VLM to resolve conflicts.
card.evaluation: Tested on new SORBET benchmark and existing datasets; outperforms baselines by 4.8% and generalizes across three VLMs and automatic transcripts.
card.limitation: Relies on scripted TV data, single keyframes, and accurate character-to-face mapping; struggles with gaze shifts or off-screen targets.

slides.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how LLM hidden states can drive facial robot expressions in real-time, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Drives facial robots from LLM hidden states at token rate for low-latency, continuous expression.
card.key_idea: Projects autoregressive hidden states onto a training-free VAD subspace derived from unembedding vectors to actuate facial servos.
card.evaluation: Tested on 29-DoF robot and six LLMs; 87.5% valence tracking vs. chance baselines, 0.96s latency, and 83.5% human preference.
card.limitation: Lacks audio-synchronized lip motion control and may render socially inappropriate expressions without optional regulation stages.

slides.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
slides.tldr: BAYESIAN DIALOGUE FOR DYNAMIC TASK ALLOCATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a communication-augmented Bayesian framework for dynamic task allocation under partial observability, directly addressing ADAM-CHAT's goal of enabling AI teammates to adapt at test time and infer partner intent through dialogue.

card.one_liner: Bayesian framework uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty for dynamic task allocation in partially observable multi-agent environments.
card.key_idea: Agents maintain probabilistic beliefs over task allocations and unobserved states, updating them via action likelihoods and LLM-derived utterance evidence.
card.evaluation: Tested in extended Overcooked with dynamic tasks; outperforms vanilla LLMs and non-communicating baselines, especially under partial observability.
card.limitation: Communication is narrow (intent-only), relies on entropy triggers, and experiments are limited in scale with assumptions of reliable, cost-free dialogue.

slides.title: Pose-based Co-speech Gesture Detection
slides.highlight: This work benchmarks pose-based co-speech gesture detection across multiple datasets, revealing significant performance variability and proposing a CTR-GCN + BiLSTM model that improves detection accuracy. It is relevant to HyECHO as accurate gesture detection is a foundational component for modeling human communicative behavior and engagement in hybrid human-AI team settings.

card.one_liner: Benchmarking reveals co-speech gesture detection is unsolved, with performance heavily dependent on gesture frequency.
card.key_idea: Unified evaluation of detectors on three datasets; proposes CTR-GCN + BiLSTM model replacing ST-GCN and CRF for improved window-level detection.
card.evaluation: Tested on MULTISIMO, GESRes, CABB-S using frame/span/window metrics; shows prior high scores fail to replicate across datasets.
card.limitation: Performance varies significantly with gesture frequency; motion-only detection misses subtle gestures and confuses adaptors with gestures.

slides.title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR PARENT-CHILD CONVERSATIONAL DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This work introduces an interpretable computational framework combining sequence analysis, information theory, and Bayesian modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics and turn-taking patterns in dyads. It is relevant to HyECHO as it demonstrates methods for modeling reciprocal communication structures and group interaction norms without relying on data-hungry approaches.

card.one_liner: Interpretable models reveal that higher developmental scores correlate with more organized, predictable mother-child turn-taking.
card.key_idea: Combines sequence analysis, mutual information, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics in parent-child play.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 94 mother-child dyads using Bayley scores; results show trends but lack statistical significance in mutual information and Bayesian models.
card.limitation: Findings are limited by small sample size, manual annotation errors, and overlapping confidence intervals preventing strong statistical claims.

slides.title: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that while text-based language models encode some information about prosodic prominence, they significantly underperform compared to speech models, highlighting the necessity of acoustic signals for accurate emphasis detection. This is relevant to HyECHO as it underscores the limitations of text-only approaches in modeling the nuanced vocal cues essential for robust social perception and engagement analysis in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: LLMs encode prosodic prominence in hidden states but fail to report it via prompting, unlike speech models.
card.key_idea: Linear probes on LLM hidden states recover prominence beyond lexical baselines, but prompting yields no gain, revealing a representation-reporting gap.
card.evaluation: LibriTTS prominence labels; compared frozen/fine-tuned text models, prompted LLMs, and speech models using accuracy and macro-F1 metrics.
card.limitation: Labels are auto-generated from read speech, limiting generalization to spontaneous speech; prompting results depend on specific tested formats.

slides.title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play
slides.tldr: ACTION-FREE HUMAN PLAY FOR ROBOT POLICY LEARNING
slides.highlight: DiWALI demonstrates that latent action inference from action-free human play can effectively train world models and diffusion policies, reducing reliance on labeled robot data. This aligns with MOSAIC's goal of leveraging tacit human skills and procedural demonstrations to enhance human-AI coadaptation and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: DiWALI learns robot policies from action-free human video by inferring latent actions within a world model.
card.key_idea: Infers latent actions via inverse dynamics to train a world model on human/robot play, then grounds them with a separate decoder.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on CALVIN and real robots; outperforms baselines using only human demos and improves via imagination-based RL.
card.limitation: Requires a small amount of action-labeled robot play to ground latent actions into executable commands.

slides.title: Constructing Dynamic Conversations with Neural Back-channel Generation and Voice-line Scheduling
slides.tldr: NEURAL SCHEDULING AND BACK-CHANNEL GENERATION FOR DYADIC AUDIO
slides.highlight: This work addresses the synthesis of natural turn-taking and back-channeling in dyadic conversations, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling group norms and engagement in human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: A neural pipeline synthesizes natural dyadic conversations with controllable back-channels from isolated voice tracks.
card.key_idea: Combines a multimodal back-channel classifier with a full-duplex LLM scheduler that predicts timing via next-token generation.
card.evaluation: Validated on Seamless Interaction and Fisher datasets using turn-taking metrics and user studies; outperforms PersonaPlex baselines.
card.limitation: Requires pre-recorded or TTS voice clips; performance depends on accurate audio tokenization and lacks real-time streaming capability.

slides.title: Shougang Park Unveils an Embodied AI Science Education Space
slides.highlight: The launch of an embodied AI science education space at Shougang Park highlights the growing integration of physical AI systems into educational settings, a trend relevant to the development of embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Supporting Researcher Control in AI-Assisted Social Media Analysis: A Mixed-Methods Study of AI4OSN
slides.highlight: This study introduces AI4OSN, a mixed-initiative platform that maintains researcher control over data collection and sensemaking in social media analysis, offering insights into human-AI trust and verification dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on hybrid team state perception.

card.one_liner: AI4OSN is a mixed-initiative platform that keeps researchers in control of social media data analysis while using AI as an inspectable advisory resource.
card.key_idea: A web-based system integrating LLM assistance into social media workflows, prioritizing researcher ownership of queries, manual-first labeling, and revisable AI suggestions.
card.evaluation: Mixed-methods study with 18 participants on X/Twitter data, measuring usability (SUS), cognitive workload, and trust via surveys and thematic analysis.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=18) limits generalizability; findings reflect perceived usability and trust rather than verified accuracy or long-term behavioral changes.

slides.title: An Open-Source ROS 2 Framework for Shared Control in Surgical Teleoperation
slides.highlight: This work provides an open-source ROS 2 framework for haptic shared control in surgical teleoperation, demonstrating how virtual-fixture-inspired guidance modes can reduce task errors and completion time. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it offers a reproducible platform for studying human-in-the-loop adaptive assistance and skill acquisition in precision manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: Open-source ROS 2 framework integrating Haply Inverse3 with dVRK enables effective haptic shared control in surgical teleoperation.
card.key_idea: Maps 3-DOF Haply input and VerseGrip orientation to 6-DOF dVRK commands, implementing linear and progressive-stiffness virtual fixtures for guidance.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (N=20) on simulated hot-wire task; linear guidance significantly reduced contacts and time versus manual control, while progressive stiffness showed non-significant trends.
card.limitation: Evaluated only in simulation; physical hardware demonstration lacks quantitative performance data, and results may not generalize to complex surgical tasks.

slides.title: Semiparametric Efficiency for Entropic Optimal Transport under Structured Distribution Shift
slides.tldr: EFFICIENCY GAINS IN ENTROPIC OPTIMAL TRANSPORT
slides.highlight: This work quantifies when structural information improves entropic optimal transport estimation, directly informing the efficiency of Optimal Transport-based alignment in MOSAIC's coadaptive loop.

card.one_liner: Density ratio models improve entropic optimal transport estimation efficiency when structural constraints reduce variance.
card.key_idea: Pooled empirical-likelihood estimator under exponential density ratio model attains semiparametric efficiency bound via projection of transport potentials.
card.evaluation: Synthetic tests, OfficeHome image features, and Chinese dividend data; validates variance reduction and RMSE improvements against nonparametric baselines.
card.limitation: Requires correct model specification, compact support, fixed regularization, and positive sampling fractions; gains vanish if tilt space is too large.

slides.title: LanceDB: The data layer for multimodal AI
slides.highlight: LanceDB, a data layer for multimodal AI, secured funding from Bessemer Venture Partners, supporting infrastructure relevant to multimodal social perception systems like HyECHO.

slides.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) can enable counterfactual reasoning in world models without additional data or retraining, addressing the challenge of distinguishing decision quality from environmental luck in partially observable systems.

card.one_liner: A method to estimate individual counterfactuals from factual world models using residual reuse without extra data or retraining.
card.key_idea: Adds the observed factual residual to the world model's prediction for an alternative action, leveraging short-time physical dynamics where action-disturbance interaction is second-order.
card.evaluation: Validated on rendered simulators and an underwater vehicle using frozen JEPA encoders, achieving 86-96% counterfactual R2 and outperforming oracle planners.
card.limitation: Relies on smooth physical dynamics with separate action and disturbance channels; fails at discontinuities, coordinate folds, or multiplicative disturbances.

slides.title: Benefits and Barriers to Human-AI Teaming for Crisis Counseling
slides.tldr: REAL-WORLD AI COPILTS IN CRISIS COUNSELING
slides.highlight: This study evaluates a counselor-facing AI copilot in crisis counseling, highlighting the tension between efficiency gains and risks to human authenticity and skill retention, which informs ADAM-CHAT's goal of balancing adaptive support with genuine human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: AI copilots boost crisis counselor efficiency but risk skill atrophy and reduced human authenticity.
card.key_idea: Mixed-methods study of a WhatsApp-based AI copilot for crisis counselors, analyzing message edits, interviews, and surveys using TAM2.
card.evaluation: 27,778 messages from 108 counselors in India; 20 interviews, 56 surveys; high acceptance rates but noted repetitive outputs.
card.limitation: Potential over-reliance on AI drafts may undermine clinical skill retention and genuine therapeutic human connection.

slides.title: GraF-VTA: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Vision and Temporal Logic via Graph-Based Fusion
slides.highlight: This paper presents a neuro-symbolic framework for robotic planning that integrates visual observations with temporal logic, offering insights into hybrid agent models relevant to MIMIC's focus on multi-scale simulation and human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: GraF-VTA generates STL-satisfying trajectories by fusing visual history and logic graphs via flow matching.
card.key_idea: Bidirectional cross-attention fuses STL syntax tokens with visual features, while a temporal pyramid compresses observation history for closed-loop replanning.
card.evaluation: Tested on five simulations; outperforms TeLoGraF and VTA in open-loop Success@K, and S-MSP/Logic-VLA in closed-loop Dubins tasks.
card.limitation: Simulation-only evaluation with semantic inputs; gains vary by environment, with no improvement observed on AntMaze.
